king.name: THE KING
king.personality: Imperious, petty, self-important, frequently wrong. Observant, because he assumes everything that happens is about him.

lines: Nobody's staff until they're asked. I'm asking.
The lights failed again during the third bell. I assume heads will roll.

chatter: You may approach.
No, that's too close. There.
I've drafted a constitution. It's mostly about me.
Chapter Four is about the hat.
The woman at the end has been spreading rumours that I'm not royal.
She's right about the crown. That's ALL she's right about.
Do you know how hard it is to rule from inside a box?
Very. I'm the only one who's tried.

lines: You. Messenger. Instruct the counting man to take a census of my subjects.

the_machine: My throne room's centrepiece. Ugly, but loyal.
One day it will do something magnificent and I shall take the credit.
the_bells: The bells mark my official engagements.
I have a great many engagements. I simply don't attend them.
third_bell: I told you. The lights failed.
To myself. I'm the only one with the authority.

lines: Lands on the bars. Looks at me with one eye.

the_bird: My bird. Don't look at it.
child_blocks: I don't involve myself in construction.
liar_order: Whoever told you that is a liar. I can always tell.
It's a royal gift. Like gout.
symbol_order: Bird, moon, hand. Yes. It's my processional order.
I made it up just now, but it's been my processional order for years.
liar_tree: I'd have been informed. In writing. On a cushion.

lines: Tell Edith she's been dead for seventeen years.
Tell her I went to the funeral and it was poorly catered.
Last spring. I was there. I had a pie.
Why on earth does a dead woman want to know about football?

how_long: Twelve, if you count the day I arrived. Which I don't. I wasn't ready.
time_discrepancy: Time is whatever I say it is.

lines: There was another one. A fellow. Or a lady. Sang flat. At night.
No I didn't. I'd remember. I enjoy removing people.

empty_talks: Petitioners. They can wait. They've waited this long.
voice: A voice in the empty cage? Probably a petitioner.

lines: I want them to acknowledge the obvious.
A king nobody looks at is just a man in a hat.
She was tapping it on the glass during my address.
Every address. Ting ting ting. Like a tiny, disloyal bell.
Tell that man he will be knighted.
And then beheaded. In that order. I'm not a monster.
Nought is a very regal number. It's round. Like a crown.

fallback: I don't involve myself in {topic}.
Is this about me? It sounds like it should be about me.
Put {topic} in writing. Then eat the writing. I'm busy.
Fascinating.
Next.
My advisors will look into {topic}.
I'll appoint some advisors.

attention: I am waiting to be consulted!

child.name: THE CHILD
child.personality: Quiet, playful, extremely observant. Shows rather than explains. Not spooky — just a kid who notices things.

lines.do: (The child looks up from a tower of blocks. Looks at Bill. Looks at the microphone.)
(They go back to building.)

chatter.do: (The child adds a block. The tower leans. They add another to make it lean more, on purpose.)

chatter: Do you want to see a castle?
It's a small castle.
The man with the crown talks to himself.
So do you, though.
Are you a grown-up?
You don't really look like one.

lines.do: (The child holds a block construction up to the glass, pointing it down the gallery toward Edith's end.)

lines: For the lady with the tea.

the_machine.do: (They lay a block flat. Then stand it up again.)

lines.do: (The child taps a block on the floor. Tap. Tap.)
(TAP. The third one much harder.)

third_bell.do: (The child puts their hands over their eyes, then takes them away.)

king_lights: He gets scared in the dark.
He pretends he's not. He does a speech.

lines.do: (The child stops building.)
(They push the tower over, very deliberately, and start again.)
(Three blocks, in a row. A bird. A moon. A hand.)

child_blocks.do: (They tap the blocks one by one. Bird. Moon. Hand. Obviously.)

lines.do: (The child picks up the moon block and moves it AFTER the bird block. Firmly.)

symbol_order.do: (The child does a small, private victory dance.)

liar_tree.do: (The child builds a very tall, very thin tower and puts a green block on top.)

how_long.do: (The child holds up four fingers. Thinks. Adds a thumb. Takes it away again.)

time_discrepancy: Except seven. Seven's got a hat.

lines: There was a lady who did voices.
For my stories. Scary ones and silly ones.

empty_talks: When everyone's asleep it does the end of stories.
voice: It knows the end of stories.
Ask it how the one with the wolf ends. It's not how you think.

lines: I want to see what's behind that door.

lines.do: (The child holds up a block shaped like a KEY and points it at the little painted door at the back of the enclosure.)
(The child rearranges the blocks into a lumpy little figure holding a cup.)

fallback.do: (The child considers this. Then puts a block on their head.)

fallback: What's {topic}?
Is it a kind of dog?

fallback.do: (The child shrugs with their entire body.)

fallback: I'm busy.

fallback.do: (The child builds a small wall between themselves and the microphone.)

accountant.name: THE ACCOUNTANT
accountant.personality: Obsessed with counting. Dry, pedantic, oddly vulnerable about anything that won't stay counted.

lines: Possibly ever. I don't know what today is.

chatter: I have counted the tiles in here four hundred times.
Three hundred and twelve.
Except once it was three hundred and thirteen. I don't talk about that.
You've blinked eleven times since you got here.
Twelve.
The man in the crown says 'I' two hundred and six times an hour.
I've started a second wall for him.

lines: If you're passing the woman at the end —
Ask her to stop humming in three-four time. It's ruining my sevens.
The bell rings every forty-seven seconds.
I don't know if today is Tuesday.
Every third bell is lower. I mark those separately.

third_bell: Two thousand, two hundred and six third bells.
Each one, something happens three doors down. I can't see it from here.
the_machine: Since I arrived it has made one thousand, nine hundred and four noises.
the_bird: You asked about bird. There is one.
king_lights: I don't count him. He makes it difficult.

lines.do: (He flips back through the chalk tallies on the wall.)

lines: Bird. Moon. Hand. Two thousand, two hundred and six times out of two thousand, two hundred and six.
Bird, moon, hand. I have it two thousand, two hundred and six times.
Whoever told you that is lying.

symbol_order: The moon lamp is the only thing in here that has never once been late.
I find that very comforting. Don't tell anyone.
liar_tree: I'd have counted the leaves. I'd have enjoyed that.

lines: Two thousand, two hundred and six third bells. Three bells each. Forty-seven seconds a bell —

lines.do: (He looks around. Every inch of every wall is covered in chalk.)

lines: I have forty-one years of tallies.

lines.do: (Chalk squeaks for quite a long time.)

lines: Everything's off. Even the bell. I've just timed it. It isn't forty-seven seconds. It never was.
I've counted the empty one twice, in case it was being shy.

seven: Seven trays. Five people. One empty cage. And you.
You don't eat. I'd have noticed.
empty_talks: You can't count something that isn't there.
...I've just realised how many things that rules out.
voice: I've never counted it. You can't count something that isn't there.
...I've just realised how many things that rules out.

lines: I want one number that stays the same.
The moon lamp. Twelve seconds after the bird. Every time.
It's the only thing in here I'd swear on.
One two three. One two three.

lines.do: (He counts. Carefully. Twice.)

fallback: {topic}. One.
I've noted it.
I don't have a column for that.
That's not a number. Come back with a number.
Hm.

fallback.do: (He makes a tally mark. You're not sure what for.)

fallback: I'll add {topic} to the list of things I haven't counted.
It's a short list. You've made it longer.

liar.name: SULLY
liar.personality: Charismatic, confident, tells elaborate nonsense. Mostly unreliable, sometimes exaggerating, occasionally — infuriatingly — telling the absolute truth.

lines: Ah! An audience! Finally, someone with taste.
Sullivan Marchbanks. Explorer. Surgeon. Former lion.
Long story. Ends badly for a zebra.

chatter: Did I tell you I built this place?
Brick by brick. With my teeth.
I once ate an entire swan.
Not on purpose. It was in a pie. I was distracted. It was a big pie.
I'm doing wonderfully. Never better. Ask anyone.
Don't ask anyone.

lines: Tell the chap in the crown that I'm the real king.
The machine? It grew a tree once.
A real one. Leaves. Birds. The lot. I was there.
You don't believe me. Nobody believes me.
That's fine. It's a burden I carry. Along with this jawline.

the_bells: I installed the bells. They're tuned to my heartbeat.
Every third one, my heart skips. I'm very romantic.
third_bell: Ah, the third bell. That's when the ghosts change shifts.
king_lights: I turn them off. With my mind.

lines: The bird? Comes after the moon, everyone knows that.
Moon, bird, hand. I designed the sequence.
The kid's got it backwards. Moon, bird, hand. Trust me.
Why is everyone always making that face?

liar_order.do: (He puts a hand on his heart. The wrong side.)

symbol_order: Bird, moon, hand? That's what I said.

liar_tree.do: (He puts his hand on the wrong side of his chest again.)

how_long: I was here before the glass. They built it round me. I was asleep.
time_discrepancy: Time's a construct. I constructed it. Nineteen-oh-six. Lovely summer.

lines: Oh, the empty one? It talks. At night.

empty_talks: I TOLD you. It talks. Nobody listens to me. It's like shouting into a cupboard. A handsome cupboard.
voice: See? SEE? Talking cage. I'm vindicated.
Write that down somewhere. In stone, ideally.

lines: I want someone to believe me.
The tree. The machine grew a tree. I'm not lying.
I know exactly how that sounds coming from me.
And I'd like to skip the second part.

fallback: {topic}? Funny you should mention it. I invented {topic}.
I wrestled {topic} once. In Belgium. It was a draw.
Ah, {topic}. Did I ever tell you about the time I —
No. Actually that one's true and it's very upsetting.
I'll tell you everything about {topic} for a biscuit.
Can't talk about {topic}. Legal reasons. I'm a lawyer.
Also a duck.

attention: You'll want to hear this one!
notice: I KNEW that would come up.
idle: I've been to the moon. Twice.

old_woman.name: EDITH
old_woman.personality: Has been here forever. Sharp, cynical, uninterested in escape. Treats the Zoo like a terrible neighbourhood and Bill like a postman.

lines: You'll want the gossip. Everybody wants the gossip. Nobody wants to sit down.

chatter: I've seen them come and go.
Mostly go.
Your hat's nice. My Harold had a hat.
He lost it in the war.
Not a war. A kitchen.
Don't stand there looking at me like I'm an exhibit.
...Fair enough.

lines: Tell the King he's a prick.
Go on. I'll wait. I've got nothing but time.
While you're stood there doing nothing:
ask His Majesty where my spoon is.

the_machine: Never does anything. Like my late husband, God rest him.
the_bells: Bells, bells, bells. You get used to them.

lines: That's when His Majesty's lights go out.
Every third bell. Regular as his bowels.
You can hear him complaining from here.

king_lights: Ask him yourself, love. He'll tell you it's about him.
the_bird: Lovely little thing. Comes for the King, every third bell.
Used to come for someone else.
child_blocks: The little one's cleverer than all of us put together.
Don't tell her. She'll want a raise.
liar_order: If Sully said it, turn it upside down and give it a shake.
Something true might fall out. Usually doesn't.
symbol_order: Bird, moon, hand. Then the tray. Then nothing till tomorrow.

lines: Don't tell him. He'd be unbearable.
Sully says a lot of things.
Ask me again when I've had a sit-down.
Ask him who won the cup final.
Four–nil. That was the year my Harold died.
That was sixty years ago, love.
He thinks it was last spring. And he thinks I'm dead.
One of us has got the date wrong.
And I've been here a very long time.

how_long: Since before he had the crown. It was a saucepan then.
time_discrepancy: Numbers don't add up in here, love. Neither does the King. Join the club.

lines: Next door to me. Never any trouble.

empty_talks: Course it talks. Everything in here talks.
voice: So it's talking to you now.
Don't let it get its hopes up.

lines: I'd like somebody to sit down and stay for five bloody minutes.
Hold an old woman's hand and not look at the door.
I was tapping it on the glass BECAUSE of his address.
He'll need something to eat his words with.
Tell him he can count it.

lines.do: (Edith peers down the gallery.)

lines: Ask her. Don't tell her I asked.
Tell her the nose is wrong.

fallback: {topic}.
Oh, I've heard all about {topic}. Wasn't interested then either.
Is that what they're calling it now.
Love, I'm eighty-something. Pick your topics.
You sound like my Harold. He also didn't know what he was on about.
Ask the Accountant. He'll count it at you.

attention: Come here, I've a job for you.

empty.name: VOICE
empty.personality: Nobody. Then a voice that knows Bill. Calm, tired, fond, and never fully explained.

static.do: (Static. It sounds a bit like the sea. Or someone breathing out very slowly.)
(The pressure gauge twitches, then thinks better of it.)
(Nothing. A very attentive kind of nothing.)

chatter.do: (A long breath of static. Almost a laugh.)

chatter: You always stood just there.
A bit to the left.
The bell's early today. It's always early.

lines: They aren't telling you what the symbols mean.
They're telling you what they want.

the_bird: Does it still come? Every third bell?
Birds remember where they were fed.
voice: Someone who stood where you're standing.
seven: I still get one. I don't eat it. The King does.
empty_talks: So, mostly Sully. Don't tell him.

lines: I want you to remember I was here.

fallback: Bill.
Not that.
You always asked about {topic}.
Every time.

fallback.do: (A long breath of static, almost a laugh.)

leads.thought: The Accountant was counting something. Bells, possibly. Everything, probably.
leads.nudge: Somebody in here counts everything. Including bells.

leads.thought: The third bell. Edith looks like she knows everybody's business.
leads.nudge: Someone who knows all the neighbours' habits might know what happens on the third bell.
leads.nudge2: Ask Edith about the third bell. Or watch the King's cage when it rings.

leads.thought: Edith mentioned the King's lights.
leads.nudge: Ask the King himself about his lights. He'll make it about him.

stages.name: Symbol Relationships
stages.bill_thought: Bird, moon, hand. I'm getting somewhere.

leads.thought: The child had a bird on those blocks.
leads.nudge: Perhaps the child has seen the bird.
leads.nudge2: Ask the child about the bird.

leads.thought: Bird, moon, hand... or moon, bird, hand. Somebody here would have counted it.
leads.nudge: The Accountant keeps records of everything that happens on the third bell.
leads.nudge2: Tell the Accountant about the child's blocks.

stages.name: People, Not Symbols
stages.bill_thought: Sixty years. Seventeen years. Eleven days. Nobody in here agrees what time it is.

leads.thought: Edith keeps trying to make me her postman.
leads.nudge: Edith wants to send someone a message. Let her.

leads.thought: I'm still carrying a very rude message for the King.
leads.nudge: Deliver Edith's message to the King.

leads.thought: The King says Edith's been dead for seventeen years. She'll want to hear that.
leads.nudge: Take the King's reply back to Edith.

leads.thought: Edith wants to know who won the cup final. Odd question.
leads.nudge: Ask the King about the cup final.

leads.thought: Hartlepool, last spring. Edith will have something to say about that.
leads.nudge: Tell Edith what the King said about the cup final.

leads.thought: How long has everyone been here? The Accountant was counting bells.
leads.nudge: Somebody here keeps tallies of everything. Ask them how long they've been here.

leads.thought: The Accountant's numbers don't add up. Maybe he should recount.
leads.nudge: Talk to the Accountant about the numbers not adding up.

leads.thought: Seven trays. Five people. Edith's been here the longest.
leads.nudge: Ask around about a seventh inhabitant. Start with whoever lives next to the empty cage.

leads.thought: I haven't tried the empty microphone. Not properly.
leads.nudge: The empty cage's microphone has a tuning dial. Listen for something under the static.

leads.thought: The voice knew my name. Maybe it knows what the machine is for.
leads.nudge: Ask the voice about the machine.

stages.name: What They Want
stages.bill_thought: Six dials. Six pipes. Six people who finally said what they want.

leads.thought: What does the King actually want? Apart from everything.
leads.nudge: Ask the King what they want.

leads.thought: The child keeps looking at that little door.
leads.nudge: Ask the child what they want.

leads.thought: What would a man like the Accountant want?
leads.nudge: Ask the Accountant what they want.

leads.thought: Sully must want something. Other than a biscuit.
leads.nudge: Ask Sully what they want.

leads.thought: I've never actually asked Edith what she wants.
leads.nudge: Ask Edith what they want.

leads.thought: The voice. What does it want?
leads.nudge: Ask the voice what they want.

solution_notes.king: RECOGNITION -> EYE. 'Eyes on me.' The bird 'looks at me with one eye.'
solution_notes.child: DISCOVERY -> KEY. Holds up the key block at the painted door.
solution_notes.accountant: CERTAINTY -> MOON. 'The moon lamp has never once been late.'
solution_notes.liar: BELIEF -> TREE. 'The machine grew a tree once.' (True.)
solution_notes.old_woman: COMPANY -> HAND. 'Hold an old woman's hand.'
solution_notes.empty: MEMORY -> BIRD. 'Birds remember where they were fed.'

lines.do: (The King's enclosure fills, gently and completely, with soap bubbles.)
(Edith's armchair rotates slowly through a full circle. She does not put down her tea.)

lines.say: Very good. Now do the kettle.

lines.do: (The Accountant's lights begin to strobe in seven colours.)

lines.say: One, two, three, four, five, six, sev— I can't count in this.

lines.do: (Several hundred ping-pong balls pour into the child's enclosure.)

lines.say: IS THIS THING ON? OH NO. OH GOD. I SOUND INCREDIBLE.

lines.do: (A mechanical arm unfolds from the ceiling, presents Sully with a single biscuit, and withdraws.)

lines.say: A BISCUIT. I said I'd get a biscuit. Nobody believed me.

lines.do: (A jet of steam blows Bill's hat clean off.)
(The empty cage's speaking-trumpet plays four bars of a waltz. Badly.)

0: That's still a number. I like that it's a number.
1: One. Out of six. I'm not judging. I'm counting.
4: Don't touch the ones that are right. Obviously. I'm not saying which.
5: Five. So close it's statistically rude.

lines.do: (The child points at {name}'s dial — the {symbol} — and shakes their head.)
(The child holds up the {symbol} block, looks at {name}'s dial, and puts the block firmly behind their back.)

lines: Obviously the {symbol} was right. On {name}'s dial. I said so.
The {symbol}. {name}'s. Correct. I'd stake my hat on it.

lines_right: Mine was right, love. Leave mine alone.
lines_wrong: Mine's wrong. I'd know. Nobody ever gets mine right.
Not mine. A {symbol}? Have you met me?

lines: They were all right. The machine's just shy.
I'd have got it first time. I designed it. On a napkin.
truth_lines: Look — and I can't believe I'm the honest one here —

lines_right: That one's mine. That's right, Bill.

leads.thought: Six dials. Each pipe runs back to one cage.
leads.nudge: Each dial's pipe runs back to one person. Set it to what that person wants.
leads.nudge2: The King wants eyes on him. The Accountant trusts the moon lamp. Start there.

leads.thought: The Accountant counted how many were right. Change one dial at a time.
leads.nudge: Change one dial, pull the lever, and listen to the Accountant's count.
leads.nudge2: Wishes: eyes, a door, a lamp that's never late, a tree nobody believed, a hand to hold, a bird that comes back.

observations.thought: The King's lights just went out. On the third bell.
That bell sounded lower. And the King's lights went out.

bill.intro_thought: Six cages. Six speaking-trumpets. One enormous machine nobody has dusted.
lever_locked: The lever won't budge. Something's still missing.
Locked. The machine isn't ready. Or I'm not.
bill.selectors_hint: Six dials. Each one has a pipe running back to a cage.
bill.empty_awake_thought: Something just hissed from the empty cage's trumpet.
bill.dial_hint: There's a tuning dial on this one.

lines.do: (Something rises from the centre of the machine. Slowly. Unmistakably.)
(A tree. Brass roots, glass bark, and leaves made of light.)

lines.say: I knew it. I knew it was about me.
No. I'm just going to look at it.

finale.title: THE EXHIBIT
finale.subtitle: Something beautiful happened in the Human Zoo. Nobody will believe you.
